title: Join the 2 million
passage: Over 2 million people now start their mornings with Thrivetide greens powder. Your neighbors, your coworkers, the folks at your gym. It's the fastest-growing wellness drink in the country, and that doesn't happen by accident. What are you waiting for? First tub 30% off.
cue: It's the fastest-growing wellness drink in the country, and that doesn't happen by accident.
explanation: The ad offers sales numbers and growth as the reason to buy, with no evidence the powder does anything for your health. Popularity can reflect marketing as easily as results.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_authority: No expert or celebrity is cited; the pitch rests entirely on how many people are buying.

passage:
Owen: Is the take-home quiz open-book? The syllabus says all quizzes are closed-book.
Leila: Literally the whole class is using their notes. If that many people are doing it, it's obviously allowed.
Owen: Or a lot of people are about to lose points.
cue: If that many people are doing it, it's obviously allowed.
explanation: Leila concludes notes are allowed because most classmates are using them. The syllabus sets the rule, and it says closed-book no matter how many people ignore it.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_tradition: Leila isn't saying it's always been done this way; she points to how many people are doing it right now.

title: Buggy, but there's a reason it's #1
passage: Setup took most of an afternoon, and the mobile app crashes whenever I attach large files. Support took four days to reply. That said, this has been the most downloaded productivity app on the store for three years running, so whatever problems it has can't be that serious. Four stars.
cue: so whatever problems it has can't be that serious
explanation: Paul lists real problems from his own use, then waves them away because the app is the most downloaded. Download counts don't make the crashes or slow support any less serious.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_authority: Paul isn't deferring to an expert; he lets the app's popularity outweigh his own evidence.

passage: I've heard from residents on both sides of this, and I know change is never comfortable. But thirty-eight towns in the region have switched to every-other-week trash pickup in the last two years, and more sign on every month. It's clear which way the region is heading, and I don't want Ferncliff to be the last town left behind.
cue: I don't want Ferncliff to be the last town left behind
explanation: Rafael's whole case is that other towns have switched and more keep joining. That shows the change is spreading, not that every-other-week pickup would work for Ferncliff's households or budget.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_tradition: Rafael isn't defending an old custom; he pushes the change because most towns are adopting it, which is popularity, not tradition.

passage: The line outside Halmeoni's Table has gone around the block every single day since it opened two weeks ago. Thirty-minute waits, sold out by 2. I haven't actually made it in yet, but at this point it's clearly the best Korean food in Wrenford. Sorry to every other spot in town.
cue: I haven't actually made it in yet, but at this point it's clearly the best
explanation: Ji-woo crowns the restaurant the best Korean food in town based on its lines, without tasting it. Crowds at a brand-new spot can reflect novelty and buzz as much as quality.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_authority: No critic or expert is involved; the verdict rests on how many people are lining up.

title: Proposal: unlimited PTO starting in Q1
passage: Hi leadership team, as we plan for next quarter, I'd like us to offer unlimited paid time off. The Larchmont Talent Survey shows 71% of companies in our sector now offer it, up from 30% just three years ago. That tells me the industry has settled the question, and unlimited paid time off is simply the better model. I've attached a draft policy for Thursday's meeting.
cue: That tells me the industry has settled the question, and unlimited paid time off is simply the better model
explanation: Monique's only reason is that most companies in the sector now offer unlimited paid time off. Its rapid spread shows a trend, not that the policy is better or that it would work for this team.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_authority: The survey is a headcount of which companies offer the policy, not an expert verdict; Monique is following the crowd, not deferring to expertise.

title: Trusted the reviews, no regrets
passage: I was torn between two hiking boots. The Cairnstep has 4,800 reviews averaging 4.7 stars, and the main complaint is that it runs small, which I handled by going up half a size. For something like comfort, thousands of people actually wearing a boot tell me more than any spec sheet. Fifty trail miles in, zero blisters.
cue: For something like comfort, thousands of people actually wearing a boot tell me more than any spec sheet
explanation: Tobias uses lots of reviews as evidence about comfort, something each wearer can judge directly, and checks the main complaint. Many independent firsthand reports are real evidence here.

whyNot.fal_bandwagon: Tobias treats popularity as evidence about something every reviewer experienced firsthand, not as proof of a claim the crowd can't judge.

title: Story hour time slot for winter
passage: Hi team, we surveyed 220 families about story hour. 64% prefer Saturday mornings, 21% weekday evenings, and the rest had no preference. Since the whole point of story hour is to reach as many families as possible, the slot most families can attend is the right one. Let's move it to Saturdays at 10 starting in January.
cue: the whole point of story hour is to reach as many families as possible
explanation: Farah uses majority preference because the question is which time families want. When the goal is attendance, what most people prefer is exactly the relevant evidence.

whyNot.fal_bandwagon: Popularity is the very thing being decided here, so counting preferences is evidence, not a substitute for it.
